purpose: Opicapone is used to help people with Parkinson's disease who are already taking levodopa and carbidopa but still have times when their symptoms come back or worsen. These periods are called 'off' episodes, and this medicine helps reduce those times so your Parkinson's symptoms are better controlled throughout the day.
how_it_works: Your body normally breaks down levodopa — the main Parkinson's medicine — too quickly, which can cause your symptoms to come and go. Opicapone blocks an enzyme called COMT that breaks down levodopa, so levodopa stays active in your body longer. Think of it like putting a stopper in a drain — it helps your levodopa last longer and work more consistently.
common_side_effects: Involuntary movements or wriggling motions (dyskinesia), constipation, low blood pressure when standing up (which can cause dizziness), dry mouth, and trouble sleeping. Some people may also notice changes in the color of their urine, which is harmless.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as this medicine may not be safe for you. It can cause or worsen involuntary movements, so your levodopa dose may need to be adjusted. Avoid stopping this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor. Be careful when standing up quickly as it can lower blood pressure. It may also rarely cause a serious condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome if stopped abruptly.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 50 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day at bedtime, at least one hour before or after your levodopa/carbidopa dose. Always take it at the same time each night and swallow the capsule whole.
